newsitem.title: INDIA: HOCKEY-AUSTRALIA HIT BACK TO LIFT GOLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: HOCKEY-AUSTRALIA HIT BACK TO LIFT GOLD CUP.

text.p: Australia thrashed South Korea 6-2 in the final of the Indira Gandhi Gold Cup women's hockey tournament on Sunday to lift the title in their first appearance.

World Cup and Olympic champions Australia, who finished second in the league standings after losing 2-1 to the Koreans on Saturday, twice came from behind to romp home by scoring five goals in the second half.

The Koreans took the initial lead through a penalty corner conversion by Cho Eun-Jung in the fifth minute and Australia equalised in the 30th minute when Katrina Powell capitalised on an Alyson Annon pass after drawing the goalkeeper.
Lee Yi-Young converted a penalty corner four minutes into the second half to give Asian champions South Korea the lead once again.
Three minutes later Kate Sage scored from Powell's move from the left flank to put Australia back on terms.

Claire Mitchell's rasping drive from the top of the scoring circle in the 46th minute gave Australia the lead for the first time and Jenny Morris consolidated it with a penalty corner conversion in the 53rd minute.
Annon capitalised on a penalty stroke in the 59th minute and then capped a fine solo by shooting on target in the 63rd minute to round off the scoring.
Yang Hui Ping's hat-trick in the first half enabled China to trounce hosts India 5-0 in the play-off to decide the third position in the five-nation tournament, with Russia finishing last.
